title: AI Agent Session Lint Rules
description: Machine-readable catalog of lint rules for AI agent session data cross-project consistency

categories.name: Session Audit
categories.description: Cross-project consistency checks using AI agent session data.

rules.description: GitHub secret set on sibling repos but not this project, according to session history. Warning, not error: the evidence is only typed/run history, and secrets set in the web UI or at org level are invisible to it.
rules.trigger: `gh secret set NAME` found in session history (typed history, plus agent-run commands from the current project's transcript) for 2+ siblings but not the current project. A command with --repo/-R binds ONLY that repo, not the directory it was typed in; --org commands bind nothing. Bodies written as $(...) or backticks are parsed as one value.
rules.message: GitHub secret "{name}" is set on {count} sibling repos ({siblings}) but not on this project

rules.description: Canonical file has diverged from sibling repos.
rules.trigger: File exists in the current project and in siblings with the same GitHub owner (all siblings when the owner is unknown) with 20-90% line overlap (50-90% for .gitignore and tsconfig.json).
rules.message: {file} has diverged from sibling repos: {sibling} ({overlap}% overlap), ...

rules.description: GitHub Actions workflow missing from this project.
rules.trigger: Workflow file exists in 2+ siblings with the same GitHub owner (all siblings when the owner is unknown) but not in the current project (which has .github).
rules.message: GitHub Actions workflow "{workflow}" exists in {count} sibling repos ({siblings}) but not in this project

rules.description: Memory file references paths that no longer exist.
rules.trigger: Claude Code memory file contains path references to files that have been deleted or moved.
rules.message: Memory "{name}" references {count} path(s) that no longer exist: {paths}

rules.trigger: Two memory files from different projects have >60% line overlap, and at least one of the pair belongs to the current project (otherwise every lint run from any repo would resurface the same unrelated cross-project duplicates).

rules.description: Same command run 3+ times consecutively in agent history.
rules.trigger: Agent history for the current project (entries lacking a project path or timestamp are excluded), grouped into sessions (by provider + session ID, split at >30-minute timestamp gaps), shows the same command 3+ times in a row within a single session segment. Only command-shaped entries take part (!bash, /slash, a known program head, or a ./path executable); prompts break runs but never match. Single-command sessions are additionally merged per provider into one stream (split at the same gaps) so rapid one-shot respawn loops are caught. The message shows the command head (first 3 words, at most 60 chars, "..." when cut), with NAME=value assignments shown as NAME=... (leading ones not counted), URL userinfo as scheme://...@ and credential-flag values (-u, -p, --user, --password, --token, --auth, --api-key, --secret) as .... On Windows the project path is matched case-insensitively.

rules.description: Cyclic command pattern detected in agent history.
rules.trigger: Within a single session segment (same provider + session ID, split at >30-minute gaps; entries lacking a project path or timestamp are excluded), command-shaped history entries show a repeating sequence of 2-3 commands (e.g. A,B,A,B) repeated 2+ times. Spans already reported by session/consecutive-repeat are not re-reported. The merged one-shot stream is not scanned for cycles. Cycle elements are shown as command heads, as in session/consecutive-repeat.

rules.description: MEMORY.md exceeds Claude Code's session-load cap. The first 200 lines / 25KB are loaded every session; anything beyond is effectively invisible to the agent.
rules.trigger: <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude>/projects/<encoded-project>/memory/MEMORY.md exceeds 200 lines OR 25,600 bytes. Numbers use en-US grouping.
rules.message: MEMORY.md has {N} lines — only the first 200 are loaded. {excess} line(s) are effectively invisible to the agent.
messageVariants: MEMORY.md is {N} bytes — only the first 25,600 bytes are loaded. ~{excess} bytes are effectively invisible.

rules.description: A fixed, non-session-scoped temp path is written and later read back.
rules.trigger: The current project's history writes a literal path under a shared temp root (/tmp, /var/tmp, $TMPDIR, $TEMP, $TMP, %TEMP%, C:/Users/*/AppData/Local/Temp, Windows/Temp, and their /c/ forms) with no per-run component, then reads the same path back. Paths under a scratchpad directory, or carrying a UUID or a 16+ hex run, are not flagged. Read verbs include cat, type, source, cp/copy source, tail, head, grep, diff and node|bash|sh|python <path>. On Windows the project path is matched case-insensitively.
rules.message: Fixed temp path "{path}" is written and later read back

rules.description: A quality gate is asserted as passing while its invocation failed, crashed or produced no output.
rules.trigger: A gate (the invoked lint/typecheck/test/build program, an npm/pnpm/yarn/bun script, a make target, or a cargo/go subcommand) errors, crashes (on an is_error run any crash signature counts; otherwise only a line-anchored banner such as Segmentation fault, FATAL ERROR:, (core dumped) or exit code 3221225477) or emits nothing — empty output counts only for tools that are not silent on success (tsc, vue-tsc and eslint are exempt) — and later agent prose in the same session claims that gate passed. The claim must name the failed gate (another gate's noun does not pair with the pass word; 'build and tests pass' counts for each) and must not be negated or stated as future intent ('make' is intent only in verb position).
rules.message: '{gate}' asserted as passing, but the invocation produced no output
messageVariants: '{gate}' asserted as passing, but the invocation reported an error
'{gate}' asserted as passing, but the invocation crashed

rules.description: Many files edited on the default branch with no intervening commit.
rules.trigger: Ten or more distinct files inside the project are written in one session while on main/master without a successful commit or branch-away in between. Creating a branch (checkout -b/-B/--orphan, switch -c/-C/--create/--force-create/--orphan, worktree add) resets at once; git switch <x> / git checkout <x> reset only when the session's next branch stamp is off the default branch. An operand naming an existing file is never a branch move, and a failed checkout or commit does not reset (except a chained git commit && git push whose full output carries git's [branch sha] line). Each session accumulates separately; a successful commit in any session clears all. The message names the branch the writes landed on.
rules.message: {count} files edited on '{branch}' with no intervening commit

rules.description: A memory cites a git SHA that does not resolve in the repository.
rules.trigger: A 7-40 character hex token outside code fences, preceded on the same line by a commit-citation cue (commit, SHA, HEAD, landed in, reverted, ...), does not resolve via git cat-file (ambiguous short SHAs count as existing). UUID members, digest prefixes, decimal ids and version fragments are excluded before resolution. A SHA attributed to another repo is not checked: a sibling name or owner/repo spec right before it joined by @ or commit/sha (specs that look like file paths do not count), or a forge commit URL for another repo (GitHub /commit/, /commits/, /tree/, /blob/, /pull/N/commits/, GitLab /-/commit/). Without a git repository, or in a shallow or partial clone, the rule reports nothing.
rules.message: Memory "{name}" cites {count} commit(s) that do not resolve in this repository: {shas}

rules.description: Measures session context spent on whole-file Reads of large files. Each result is re-sent as prompt context (cache reads) on every later turn of its session; the finding is a baseline for judging read-routing changes, reported as one summary per project.
rules.trigger: One or more whole-file Read calls (no offset, limit or pages) in the current project's transcripts whose result is 4,000 tokens or more; sidechain (subagent) Reads are not counted. Carry is each result's tokens times the later turns of its session that re-sent it, up to the session's end or its next /compact boundary; a turn is a distinct assistant message id.
rules.message: {count} whole-file Reads of 4,000+ tokens ({tokens} tokens); est. {carry} tokens of cache-read carry on later turns

dataSources.name: Claude Code
dataSources.notes: Read from CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR instead of ~/.claude when it is set. Transcripts are read for the current project only, capped at the 5 most recent files and 200,000 lines (newest lines kept).

dataSources.name: Codex CLI
dataSources.notes: History lines are {session_id, ts (unix seconds), text}; Codex records no project path for them.

dataSources.name: Aider
dataSources.notes: History file is per-project, stored in the project root.

dataSources.name: Amazon Q Developer
dataSources.notes: Semi-documented; file layout inferred from observation.

dataSources.name: Goose
dataSources.notes: Requires SQLite dependency to read session data.

dataSources.name: Windsurf
dataSources.notes: Partially documented; format marked unstable by vendor.
